_Comment_DataDir: Root directory for persistent state. Subfolders are created automatically: cache/ (DNS, SMTP, HTTP probes) and auth/ (users.json).
_Comment_CacheDir: OMITTED ON PURPOSE — the key is left out rather than set to null, because a JSON null binds to the empty string. Where probe results are persisted; defaults to {DataDir}/cache. Set it to "none" to turn the disk tier off entirely (memory + Redis only). On a multi-pod deployment WITH Redis, point it at a pod-local volume (emptyDir) instead: Redis already shares results between pods, and keeping the cache local removes all cross-pod file traffic from the shared mount and makes startup I/O O(1) per pod rather than scaling with replica count. See docs/caching-architecture.md.
_Comment_CacheTtlHours: How long a persisted probe result stays usable. 0 disables expiry, but files are still swept after 24 hours: every flush appends a new file, so without a retention floor the directory would grow without bound even though memory stays flat. Also drives the in-memory cache expiry. With FlushIntervalSeconds this sets the number of live cache files per instance: TTL / interval + 1, so 13 at the defaults.
_Comment_FlushIntervalSeconds: How often newly-fetched results are written out. This is the only flush trigger, and each flush writes one immutable file, so it is also the file granularity. An ungraceful crash loses at most this much cache; a graceful shutdown flushes.
_Comment_CacheShutdownFlushSeconds: Upper bound on the final flush at shutdown, so a slow or wedged mount cannot hold the process past its termination grace period.
_Comment_DnsCacheMinTtlSeconds: 0 (default) = off: every cached DNS answer gets the full CacheTtlHours. Above zero, answers are bounded by their own record TTLs instead, as clamp(minimum record TTL, this floor, CacheTtlHours). The floor stops domains publishing 30-second records from forcing a refetch on nearly every validation.
_Comment_ProbeTuning: Optional startup-only tuning of the DNS/SMTP/HTTP probe engines. Read once when the singleton probe services are built, so a RESTART is required for changes to take effect (unlike the runtime probe data lists in config.json, which are hot-editable from the Config page). Omit any key to keep the default shown below. Dns:QueryTimeoutSeconds/QueryRetries apply to the main + direct resolvers only; the fast DNSBL/speculative resolvers keep their fixed 3s/1-retry skip-if-slow budget. See docs/configuration.md -> Probe tuning.
_Comment_Auth: Token hash for the root 'ednsv' user. Set to 'none' (the default) to disable token authentication — but a server with NO auth method enabled (no token hash, no Auth:Oidc, no Auth:JwtBearer) refuses to start unless it is bound to localhost only (see docs/configuration.md). Otherwise, generate a random secret and store ONLY its hash here. IMPORTANT: the root token is hashed with a single unsalted SHA-256, so it MUST be high-entropy — use a cryptographically random value of at least 128 bits (>= 22 base64url / 32 hex chars); never a human-chosen password. Hash algorithm: base64url(sha256(utf8-bytes(token))) — no BOM, no padding ('=' stripped, '+'->'-', '/'->'_'). Example: TOKEN=$(openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='); echo "token=$TOKEN"; printf %s "$TOKEN" | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | basenc --base64url | tr -d '='. The environment variable EDNSV_AUTH_TOKEN_HASH overrides this setting.
_Comment_AuthExternal: Optional external-IdP auth, runs alongside token auth (enable either or both). Auth:Oidc adds interactive single sign-on for the UI (any OIDC-compliant IdP; for Entra ID use Authority https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/v2.0 and see docs/entra-setup.md). The default sign-in flow (ResponseType id_token) needs NO client secret or certificate — nothing to expire or rotate; ClientSecret (or env var EDNSV_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, which overrides it) is only needed if you switch ResponseType to 'code'. Auth:JwtBearer accepts IdP-issued OAuth2 access tokens (e.g. Entra client credentials) on Authorization: Bearer for service accounts. Full key reference: docs/configuration.md.
